algorithm.title: Calculating relative risk reduction (RRR) in clinical trials

nodes.text: Identify event rates: rate in control group (CER = 26%) and rate in intervention group (EER = 13%)

Calculate relative risk reduction: RRR = (CER - EER) / CER = 50%
**Absolute risk reduction (ARR):** ARR = CER - EER = 26% - 13% = 13%
**Number needed to treat (NNT):** NNT = 1 / ARR = 1 / 0.13 = 7.7 patients

algorithm.title: Epidemiologic measures of association and excess risk

nodes.text: Cohort studies follow exposed and unexposed groups longitudinally to determine disease incidence
Incidence in exposed group: cases among exposed divided by total exposed individuals
Incidence in unexposed group: cases among unexposed divided by total unexposed individuals
Attributable risk (risk difference): excess risk in exposed calculated as exposed incidence minus unexposed incidence
**Relative risk (risk ratio):** ratio of incidence in exposed to unexposed
**Attributable risk percent (ARP):** proportion of disease in exposed attributable to exposure: (RR - 1) / RR
**Number needed to harm (NNH):** reciprocal of the attributable risk (1 / AR)

algorithm.title: Calculation and interpretation of relative risk

nodes.text: Prospective cohort studies follow exposed and unexposed groups to calculate disease incidence rates
Calculate incidence in the exposed group: cases in exposed divided by total exposed individuals
Calculate incidence in the unexposed group: cases in unexposed divided by total unexposed individuals
Relative risk (risk ratio) = incidence in exposed divided by incidence in unexposed
**Relative risk < 1.0:** exposure is associated with decreased risk of outcome (protective factor)
**Relative risk = 1.0:** null hypothesis accepted; no association between exposure and outcome
**Relative risk > 1.0:** exposure is associated with increased risk of outcome (harmful factor)

algorithm.title: Calculation of absolute risk reduction and number needed to treat

nodes.text: Randomized controlled trials evaluate therapeutic efficacy by comparing event rates between intervention and control
Event rate in the control group: events in control divided by total control subjects
Event rate in the treatment group: events in treatment divided by total treatment subjects
Absolute risk reduction (ARR): difference in event rates between groups calculated as control minus treatment
Number needed to treat (NNT): number of patients treated to prevent one adverse event (NNT = 1 / ARR)
**Number needed to harm (NNH):** reciprocal of the absolute risk increase for adverse side effects
Always round NNT up to the nearest whole integer to avoid overestimating clinical benefit

nodes.text: Screening programs aim to detect asymptomatic disease early to reduce disease-specific mortality
Length-time bias: screening preferentially detects indolent, slowly progressive tumors with long preclinical phases
Result of length-time bias: overestimation of survival and screening benefit compared to aggressive interval cancers
**Lead-time bias:** early detection advances diagnosis date without prolonging actual survival
**Overdiagnosis bias:** detection of non-progressive lesions that would never have caused clinical disease
**Selection bias (healthy volunteer bias):** individuals adhering to screening have healthier baseline lifestyle habits
Randomized controlled trials with disease-specific mortality endpoints are required to prove screening benefit
